content_html:
When I started building agent-exec-trace, I thought I knew where the difficulty would be. OSS agent-exec-trace is an observability layer for AI agents. It instruments agent runs using OpenTelemetry-style traces, then analyzes those traces for loops, retry storms, cost spikes, hallucination patterns, and other bad runtime behavior. The goal is simple: when an agent run feels wrong, I want something better than logs and intuition to explain why.

I thought the hard part would be the detector logic.

Define the anomalies. Pick the thresholds. Wire the traces. Run the analytics. Ship the repo.

That was the clean version of the story.

The real version was uglier.

On my first large pass over 100,000 real agent traces from Hugging Face, my empty_response detector fired on 100% of them. Every trace. At the same time, 28 of my 35 rule-based detectors never fired at all.

That is the moment the project stopped being "build some detectors" and turned into a learning experience.

The detectors were not wrong.

The traces were the wrong shape.

And once I saw that, a bunch of other assumptions broke with it.

I had a very similar feeling when I shipped my agent eval harness. Different tool. Same pattern. Real systems are very good at ruining tidy design stories.

What I Was Actually Trying To Build

The problem I cared about felt pretty obvious.

Traditional observability can tell me if a service is up, slow, or failing.

It cannot tell me why an agent called the same tool eight times, changed its mind three times, burned tokens on a dead-end path, or quietly drifted into behavior I would never want repeated in production.

That gap matters more than people admit.

Most teams can tell you the run felt wrong. Very few can point to the exact step where it started going wrong.

So I built agent-exec-trace: an OpenTelemetry-style observability layer for agent behavior.

The idea is simple enough to explain.

Instrument the run. Capture the behavioral path. Emit spans for planning, tool calls, retrieval, memory, approvals, and cost. Then run detectors over those traces and surface the bad runs in a UI someone can actually use.

The repo is here: github.com/deghosal-2026/agent-exec-trace

It ships as three PyPI packages, has 794 Python tests and 34 Playwright end-to-end tests, and the SDK is deliberately small enough that someone can wrap a real agent without redesigning their system.

from agent_exec_trace import AgentTracer, trace_agent, tool_span

AgentTracer.setup(otlp_endpoint="http://localhost:4317")

@trace_agent(agent_name="my-agent", agent_version="1.0.0")
async def handle(query: str) -> str:
    with tool_span("search", tool_args={"q": query}):
        return await search(query)

That part was not the lesson.

The lesson was what happened after I had something real enough to test.

The First Thing I Learned: Real Traces Fight Back

I did plan field testing.

Just not early enough.

That distinction matters, because the mistake was not forgetting it. The mistake was scheduling it late enough that the rest of the system had already started to feel done.

The WBS was solid. The PRD was thorough. The detector catalog was documented. The milestones were real. The quality gates were strict: ruff clean, mypy strict clean, tests green, coverage above 90%.

All of that was good discipline.

None of it protected me from the fact that mock agents are polite and real traces are not.

That is what "too late" looked like in practice. By the time field testing showed up, parts of the detector catalog, the assumptions about trace shape, and even some milestone gates already felt validated. Field testing did not arrive early enough to shape the design. It arrived late enough to expose where the design had been validated against the wrong reality.

The Hugging Face corpus was the first slap.

My detector expected response content in one place. The corpus stored it in many different shapes. So empty_response was not telling me "all these agents are broken." It was telling me "your assumptions about trace shape are too narrow."

That one bug forced four normalization passes. Different response keys. Different tool-name conventions. Different operation names. Timestamp parsing issues. Parent-child inconsistencies.

Bad validation data does not just create noise. It teaches you the wrong lessons with confidence.

By the end of that cleanup, the headline got more honest and less comforting.

The original compatibility number looked decent.

The real one was 42.4%.

That was the moment I stopped thinking about observability as a detector problem and started thinking about it as a data-shape problem.

Because a detector that is perfectly correct in theory is still useless if the data it depends on almost never exists in the wild.

The Second Thing I Learned: Synthetic Data Can Save You And Mislead You

Once the real-trace corpus showed me its limits, I went in the other direction.

I built a synthetic trace generator.

One million traces. Ten fake agents. Fourteen tools. Deliberate behavior modes: loops, retries, timeouts, inactivity gaps, intervention waits, token explosions, memory bursts.

That solved one problem immediately.

Structural compatibility jumped to 99.2%.

Now the detectors had something they could actually see.

Twenty of the 35 rule-based detectors fired.

That sounds like a win. And it was.

But synthetic data lies in a different way.

My hallucination detector fired on 98% of synthetic traces. Not because I had accidentally built the greatest detector in history, but because the synthetic outputs and the synthetic tool evidence had a fake relationship that made the detector's job too easy.

The same thing happened with cost. My cost_spike detector had a real threshold. My synthetic generator produced mostly cents-level costs. So the detector almost never fired there either.

Synthetic traces can prove a detector runs. They cannot prove it matters.

That gave me a second lesson I needed badly:

Synthetic traces are great for proving a detector can run.

They are not enough to prove a detector is calibrated for reality.

So now I think of validation in layers.

Unit tests tell me the logic works.

Synthetic traces tell me the detector can see the fields it needs.

Real traces tell me whether any of this matters outside my own sandbox.

That sequencing sounds obvious when written down. It did not feel obvious when I was in the middle of building it.

The Third Thing I Learned: Green Gates Can Lie

This one annoyed me more than any detector bug.

I had marked the OTLP export milestone done.

The gate was green.

The docs looked fine.

The demo looked fine.

And the end-to-end export path had never actually been verified.

Two bugs had cancelled each other out.

The OTel collector's gRPC port was not exposed in Docker Compose.

And the SDK path I was using configured local tracing instead of OTLP export.

So I had a completed milestone for a feature that had not really worked.

That was a worse lesson than a failing test.

A failing test is honest.

A green gate created by two cancelling bugs is dishonest in a way that looks disciplined.

That changed how I think about milestones.

I trust a green checkmark a lot less now.

If the gate cannot prove that a real agent emits, Jaeger receives, analytics ingests, and the API serves the result, then the gate is incomplete. I do not care how many sub-checks passed before it.

That is not an observability lesson only. That is just software engineering.

The Fourth Thing I Learned: Structure Without Content Is Not Enough

I started fairly conservative on privacy.

Metadata-only felt responsible.

No raw tool arguments. No full tool responses. No memory values by default.

Reasonable instinct.

But it taught me a more uncomfortable tradeoff.

An observability SDK that only captures structure can become blind in exactly the places where you most want judgment.

My hallucination detector is the clearest example.

If the detector cannot see what the tool returned, it cannot meaningfully judge whether the agent's claim matches the evidence.

Once I allowed truncated content instead of metadata-only, the hallucination false-positive rate dropped sharply.

That did not make the privacy question go away.

It just made the tradeoff explicit.

"Safer by default" and "useful by default" are not always the same choice.

Structure without enough evidence is just a cleaner way to stay blind.

I do not think enough tooling says that out loud.

The Fifth Thing I Learned: Shipping OSS Is Not The Same As Finishing The Idea

The repo is public.

The packages are published.

The test suite is real.

The product works.

And I still would not call the problem solved.

That matters to me.

I think too many OSS launch posts flatten everything into "here is what shipped" and skip "here is what I still do not trust."

Here is what I still do not trust fully:

  • the 28 detectors that have not yet fired on real corpora in a meaningful way
  • the LLM detectors on production workloads
  • span-tree materialization in the API, which is still weaker than I want
  • any claim that one threshold set will generalize cleanly across workloads
  • any green gate that has not been proven end-to-end

That does not mean the project should not ship.

It means the honest version of shipping is: this tool is useful now, and I understand its edges much better than I did when I started.

That is a good outcome.

It is also a very different outcome from the clean version I had in my head.

What I Would Do Differently Next Time

I would move field testing much earlier.

Not because I failed to think of it, but because planning it and planning it early are not the same thing.

Late field testing turns into audit. Early field testing shapes the design.

By the time mine ran, it was strong enough to expose bad assumptions, but too late to stop me from building confidence on top of them.

I would treat the trace corpus as a design artifact, not just test input.

I would insist on an end-to-end smoke path much earlier.

And I would stop pretending that detector logic is the center of the problem.

It matters, obviously.

But after building this, I think the harder questions are:

  • what can your traces actually see?
  • how weird is the data in the wild?
  • what does your detector depend on structurally?
  • and how do you know a green gate is real?

That is the actual education this project gave me.

Not "how to write 40 detectors."

More like: how many other things have to be true before 40 detectors mean anything.

And maybe the hardest takeaway of all: a detector that has never fired on a real trace is not really finished. It is just well tested.

Open For Discussion

I would genuinely love practitioner pushback on this.

  • If you are running agents today, what do you actually use when a run feels wrong?
  • Have you ever had a green gate that passed for the wrong reason?
  • And if you are building agent tooling, where did your clean version of the story break first?

blocks.html_en: The First Thing I Learned: Real Traces Fight Back

sentences.en: The First Thing I Learned: Real Traces Fight Back
sentences.zh: 我学到的第一件事：真实痕迹的反击

blocks.html_en: I did plan field testing.

sentences.en: I did plan field testing.
sentences.zh: 我确实计划了现场测试。

blocks.html_en: Just not early enough.

sentences.en: Just not early enough.
sentences.zh: 只是还不够早。

blocks.html_en: That distinction matters, because the mistake was not forgetting it. The mistake was scheduling it late enough that the rest of the system had already started to feel done.

sentences.en: That distinction matters, because the mistake was not forgetting it.
sentences.zh: 这种区别很重要，因为错误不是忘记它。

sentences.en: The mistake was scheduling it late enough that the rest of the system had already started to feel done.
sentences.zh: 错误在于将其安排得太晚，以至于系统的其余部分已经开始感觉已经完成了。

blocks.html_en: The WBS was solid. The PRD was thorough. The detector catalog was documented. The milestones were real. The quality gates were strict: ruff clean, mypy strict clean, tests green, coverage above 90%.

sentences.en: The WBS was solid.
sentences.zh: WBS 很可靠。

sentences.en: The PRD was thorough.
sentences.zh: PRD 很彻底。

sentences.en: The detector catalog was documented.
sentences.zh: 探测器目录已记录。

sentences.en: The milestones were real.
sentences.zh: 这些里程碑是真实的。

sentences.en: The quality gates were strict: ruff clean, mypy strict clean, tests green, coverage above 90%.
sentences.zh: 质量关卡很严格：ruff clean、mypy strict clean、测试绿色、覆盖率超过90%。

blocks.html_en: All of that was good discipline.

sentences.en: All of that was good discipline.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是良好的纪律。

blocks.html_en: None of it protected me from the fact that mock agents are polite and real traces are not.

sentences.en: None of it protected me from the fact that mock agents are polite and real traces are not.
sentences.zh: 这些都没有让我免受这样一个事实：模拟特工很有礼貌，而真实的痕迹则不然。

blocks.html_en: That is what "too late" looked like in practice. By the time field testing showed up, parts of the detector catalog, the assumptions about trace shape, and even some milestone gates already felt validated. Field testing did not arrive early enough to shape the design. It arrived late enough to expose where the design had been validated against the wrong reality.

sentences.en: That is what "too late" looked like in practice.
sentences.zh: 这就是实践中“为时已晚”的情况。

sentences.en: By the time field testing showed up, parts of the detector catalog, the assumptions about trace shape, and even some milestone gates already felt validated.
sentences.zh: 当现场测试出现时，探测器目录的部分内容、有关迹线形状的假设，甚至一些里程碑门已经得到验证。

sentences.en: Field testing did not arrive early enough to shape the design.
sentences.zh: 现场测试来得不够早，无法形成设计。

sentences.en: It arrived late enough to expose where the design had been validated against the wrong reality.
sentences.zh: 它来得太晚了，以至于暴露了设计在错误的现实中被验证的地方。

blocks.html_en: The Hugging Face corpus was the first slap.

sentences.en: The Hugging Face corpus was the first slap.
sentences.zh: 拥抱脸语料库是第一巴掌。

blocks.html_en: My detector expected response content in one place. The corpus stored it in many different shapes. So empty_response was not telling me "all these agents are broken." It was telling me "your assumptions about trace shape are too narrow."

sentences.en: My detector expected response content in one place.
sentences.zh: 我的检测器期望在一处响应内容。

sentences.en: The corpus stored it in many different shapes.
sentences.zh: 语料库以多种不同的形式存储它。

sentences.en: So empty_response was not telling me "all these agents are broken."
sentences.zh: 所以empty_response并没有告诉我“所有这些代理都坏了”。

sentences.en: It was telling me "your assumptions about trace shape are too narrow."
sentences.zh: 它告诉我“你对迹线形状的假设太狭窄了。”

blocks.html_en: That one bug forced four normalization passes. Different response keys. Different tool-name conventions. Different operation names. Timestamp parsing issues. Parent-child inconsistencies.

sentences.en: That one bug forced four normalization passes.
sentences.zh: 这个错误迫使四次标准化通过。

sentences.en: Different response keys.
sentences.zh: 不同的响应键。

sentences.en: Different tool-name conventions.
sentences.zh: 不同的工具名称约定。

sentences.en: Different operation names.
sentences.zh: 不同的操作名称。

sentences.en: Timestamp parsing issues.
sentences.zh: 时间戳解析问题。

sentences.en: Parent-child inconsistencies.
sentences.zh: 亲子关系不一致。

blocks.html_en: Bad validation data does not just create noise. It teaches you the wrong lessons with confidence.

sentences.en: Bad validation data does not just create noise.
sentences.zh: 错误的验证数据不仅会产生噪音。

sentences.en: It teaches you the wrong lessons with confidence.
sentences.zh: 它充满信心地教给你错误的教训。

blocks.html_en: By the end of that cleanup, the headline got more honest and less comforting.

sentences.en: By the end of that cleanup, the headline got more honest and less comforting.
sentences.zh: 清理结束后，标题变得更加诚实，不再那么令人安慰。

blocks.html_en: The original compatibility number looked decent.

sentences.en: The original compatibility number looked decent.
sentences.zh: 原来的兼容性数字看起来不错。

blocks.html_en: The real one was 42.4%.

sentences.en: The real one was 42.4%.
sentences.zh: 真实的比例是42.4%。

blocks.html_en: That was the moment I stopped thinking about observability as a detector problem and started thinking about it as a data-shape problem.

sentences.en: That was the moment I stopped thinking about observability as a detector problem and started thinking about it as a data-shape problem.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我不再将可观测性视为检测器问题，而是开始将其视为数据形状问题。

blocks.html_en: Because a detector that is perfectly correct in theory is still useless if the data it depends on almost never exists in the wild.

sentences.en: Because a detector that is perfectly correct in theory is still useless if the data it depends on almost never exists in the wild.
sentences.zh: 因为如果它所依赖的数据几乎不存在于野外，那么理论上完全正确的探测器仍然毫无用处。

blocks.html_en: The Second Thing I Learned: Synthetic Data Can Save You And Mislead You

sentences.en: The Second Thing I Learned: Synthetic Data Can Save You And Mislead You
sentences.zh: 我学到的第二件事：合成数据可以拯救你并误导你

blocks.html_en: Once the real-trace corpus showed me its limits, I went in the other direction.

sentences.en: Once the real-trace corpus showed me its limits, I went in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 一旦真实痕迹语料库向我展示了它的局限性，我就转向了另一个方向。

blocks.html_en: I built a synthetic trace generator.

sentences.en: I built a synthetic trace generator.
sentences.zh: 我构建了一个合成跟踪生成器。

blocks.html_en: One million traces. Ten fake agents. Fourteen tools. Deliberate behavior modes: loops, retries, timeouts, inactivity gaps, intervention waits, token explosions, memory bursts.

sentences.en: One million traces.
sentences.zh: 一百万条痕迹。

sentences.en: Ten fake agents.
sentences.zh: 十个假特工。

sentences.en: Fourteen tools.
sentences.zh: 十四个工具。

sentences.en: Deliberate behavior modes: loops, retries, timeouts, inactivity gaps, intervention waits, token explosions, memory bursts.
sentences.zh: 故意行为模式：循环、重试、超时、不活动间隙、干预等待、令牌爆炸、内存突发。

blocks.html_en: That solved one problem immediately.

sentences.en: That solved one problem immediately.
sentences.zh: 这立即解决了一个问题。

blocks.html_en: Structural compatibility jumped to 99.2%.

sentences.en: Structural compatibility jumped to 99.2%.
sentences.zh: 结构兼容性跃升至99.2%。

blocks.html_en: Now the detectors had something they could actually see.

sentences.en: Now the detectors had something they could actually see.
sentences.zh: 现在探测器有了他们可以实际看到的东西。

blocks.html_en: Twenty of the 35 rule-based detectors fired.

sentences.en: Twenty of the 35 rule-based detectors fired.
sentences.zh: 35 个基于规则的探测器中有 20 个被发射。

blocks.html_en: That sounds like a win. And it was.

sentences.en: That sounds like a win.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是一场胜利。

sentences.en: And it was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

blocks.html_en: But synthetic data lies in a different way.

sentences.en: But synthetic data lies in a different way.
sentences.zh: 但合成数据却以不同的方式存在。

blocks.html_en: My hallucination detector fired on 98% of synthetic traces. Not because I had accidentally built the greatest detector in history, but because the synthetic outputs and the synthetic tool evidence had a fake relationship that made the detector's job too easy.

sentences.en: My hallucination detector fired on 98% of synthetic traces.
sentences.zh: 我的幻觉探测器探测到了 98% 的合成痕迹。

sentences.en: Not because I had accidentally built the greatest detector in history, but because the synthetic outputs and the synthetic tool evidence had a fake relationship that made the detector's job too easy.
sentences.zh: 不是因为我无意中构建了历史上最伟大的探测器，而是因为合成输出和合成工具证据之间存在虚假关系，使得探测器的工作变得过于简单。

blocks.html_en: The same thing happened with cost. My cost_spike detector had a real threshold. My synthetic generator produced mostly cents-level costs. So the detector almost never fired there either.

sentences.en: The same thing happened with cost.
sentences.zh: 成本方面也发生了同样的情况。

sentences.en: My cost_spike detector had a real threshold.
sentences.zh: 我的 cost_spike 检测器有一个真正的阈值。

sentences.en: My synthetic generator produced mostly cents-level costs.
sentences.zh: 我的合成发电机产生的成本大部分是美分级的。

sentences.en: So the detector almost never fired there either.
sentences.zh: 所以探测器也几乎从未在那里发射过。

blocks.html_en: Synthetic traces can prove a detector runs. They cannot prove it matters.

sentences.en: Synthetic traces can prove a detector runs.
sentences.zh: 合成痕迹可以证明探测器正在运行。

sentences.en: They cannot prove it matters.
sentences.zh: 他们无法证明这很重要。

blocks.html_en: That gave me a second lesson I needed badly:

sentences.en: That gave me a second lesson I needed badly:
sentences.zh: 这给了我第二堂我急需的课：

blocks.html_en: Synthetic traces are great for proving a detector can run.

sentences.en: Synthetic traces are great for proving a detector can run.
sentences.zh: 合成迹线非常适合证明探测器可以运行。

blocks.html_en: They are not enough to prove a detector is calibrated for reality.

sentences.en: They are not enough to prove a detector is calibrated for reality.
sentences.zh: 它们不足以证明探测器已针对现实进行了校准。

blocks.html_en: So now I think of validation in layers.

sentences.en: So now I think of validation in layers.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我想到了分层验证。

blocks.html_en: Unit tests tell me the logic works.

sentences.en: Unit tests tell me the logic works.
sentences.zh: 单元测试告诉我逻辑是有效的。

blocks.html_en: Synthetic traces tell me the detector can see the fields it needs.

sentences.en: Synthetic traces tell me the detector can see the fields it needs.
sentences.zh: 合成痕迹告诉我探测器可以看到它需要的字段。

blocks.html_en: Real traces tell me whether any of this matters outside my own sandbox.

sentences.en: Real traces tell me whether any of this matters outside my own sandbox.
sentences.zh: 真实的痕迹告诉我这些在我自己的沙箱之外是否重要。

blocks.html_en: That sequencing sounds obvious when written down. It did not feel obvious when I was in the middle of building it.

sentences.en: That sequencing sounds obvious when written down.
sentences.zh: 当写下来时，这个顺序听起来很明显。

sentences.en: It did not feel obvious when I was in the middle of building it.
sentences.zh: 当我正在构建它的时候，感觉并不明显。

blocks.html_en: The Third Thing I Learned: Green Gates Can Lie

sentences.en: The Third Thing I Learned: Green Gates Can Lie
sentences.zh: 我学到的第三件事：绿色之门可能会说谎

blocks.html_en: This one annoyed me more than any detector bug.

sentences.en: This one annoyed me more than any detector bug.
sentences.zh: 这个问题比任何探测器错误都更让我恼火。

blocks.html_en: I had marked the OTLP export milestone done.

sentences.en: I had marked the OTLP export milestone done.
sentences.zh: 我已将 OTLP 导出里程碑标记为已完成。

blocks.html_en: The gate was green.

sentences.en: The gate was green.
sentences.zh: 大门是绿色的。

blocks.html_en: The docs looked fine.

sentences.en: The docs looked fine.
sentences.zh: 文档看起来不错。

blocks.html_en: The demo looked fine.

sentences.en: The demo looked fine.
sentences.zh: 演示看起来不错。

blocks.html_en: And the end-to-end export path had never actually been verified.

sentences.en: And the end-to-end export path had never actually been verified.
sentences.zh: 而且端到端的导出路径从未被实际验证过。

blocks.html_en: Two bugs had cancelled each other out.

sentences.en: Two bugs had cancelled each other out.
sentences.zh: 两个 bug 互相抵消了。

blocks.html_en: The OTel collector's gRPC port was not exposed in Docker Compose.

sentences.en: The OTel collector's gRPC port was not exposed in Docker Compose.
sentences.zh: OTel 收集器的 gRPC 端口未在 Docker Compose 中公开。

blocks.html_en: And the SDK path I was using configured local tracing instead of OTLP export.

sentences.en: And the SDK path I was using configured local tracing instead of OTLP export.
sentences.zh: 我使用配置的本地跟踪而不是 OTLP 导出的 SDK 路径。

blocks.html_en: So I had a completed milestone for a feature that had not really worked.

sentences.en: So I had a completed milestone for a feature that had not really worked.
sentences.zh: 因此，我为一项尚未真正发挥作用的功能完成了里程碑。

blocks.html_en: That was a worse lesson than a failing test.

sentences.en: That was a worse lesson than a failing test.
sentences.zh: 这是比考试失败更糟糕的教训。

blocks.html_en: A failing test is honest.

sentences.en: A failing test is honest.
sentences.zh: 失败的测试是诚实的。

blocks.html_en: A green gate created by two cancelling bugs is dishonest in a way that looks disciplined.

sentences.en: A green gate created by two cancelling bugs is dishonest in a way that looks disciplined.
sentences.zh: 由两个取消错误创建的绿色门在某种程度上看起来是不诚实的。

blocks.html_en: That changed how I think about milestones.

sentences.en: That changed how I think about milestones.
sentences.zh: 这改变了我对里程碑的看法。

blocks.html_en: I trust a green checkmark a lot less now.

sentences.en: I trust a green checkmark a lot less now.
sentences.zh: 我现在不再信任绿色复选标记了。

blocks.html_en: If the gate cannot prove that a real agent emits, Jaeger receives, analytics ingests, and the API serves the result, then the gate is incomplete. I do not care how many sub-checks passed before it.

sentences.en: If the gate cannot prove that a real agent emits, Jaeger receives, analytics ingests, and the API serves the result, then the gate is incomplete.
sentences.zh: 如果门无法证明真实代理发出、Jaeger 接收、分析摄取以及 API 提供结果，则门是不完整的。

sentences.en: I do not care how many sub-checks passed before it.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎之前通过了多少次检查。

blocks.html_en: That is not an observability lesson only. That is just software engineering.

sentences.en: That is not an observability lesson only.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一个可观察性的课程。

sentences.en: That is just software engineering.
sentences.zh: 这只是软件工程。

blocks.html_en: The Fourth Thing I Learned: Structure Without Content Is Not Enough

sentences.en: The Fourth Thing I Learned: Structure Without Content Is Not Enough
sentences.zh: 我学到的第四件事：没有内容的结构是不够的

blocks.html_en: I started fairly conservative on privacy.

sentences.en: I started fairly conservative on privacy.
sentences.zh: 我一开始对隐私相当保守。

blocks.html_en: Metadata-only felt responsible.

sentences.en: Metadata-only felt responsible.
sentences.zh: 仅元数据感到有责任。

blocks.html_en: No raw tool arguments. No full tool responses. No memory values by default.

sentences.en: No raw tool arguments.
sentences.zh: 没有原始工具参数。

sentences.en: No full tool responses.
sentences.zh: 没有完整的工具响应。

sentences.en: No memory values by default.
sentences.zh: 默认情况下没有内存值。

blocks.html_en: Reasonable instinct.

sentences.en: Reasonable instinct.
sentences.zh: 合理的本能。

blocks.html_en: But it taught me a more uncomfortable tradeoff.

sentences.en: But it taught me a more uncomfortable tradeoff.
sentences.zh: 但它教会了我一个更不舒服的权衡。

blocks.html_en: An observability SDK that only captures structure can become blind in exactly the places where you most want judgment.

sentences.en: An observability SDK that only captures structure can become blind in exactly the places where you most want judgment.
sentences.zh: 仅捕获结构的可观察性 SDK 可能会在您最需要判断的地方变得盲目。

blocks.html_en: My hallucination detector is the clearest example.

sentences.en: My hallucination detector is the clearest example.
sentences.zh: 我的幻觉探测器就是最明显的例子。

blocks.html_en: If the detector cannot see what the tool returned, it cannot meaningfully judge whether the agent's claim matches the evidence.

sentences.en: If the detector cannot see what the tool returned, it cannot meaningfully judge whether the agent's claim matches the evidence.
sentences.zh: 如果检测器无法看到工具返回的内容，则无法有意义地判断特工的声明是否与证据相符。

blocks.html_en: Once I allowed truncated content instead of metadata-only, the hallucination false-positive rate dropped sharply.

sentences.en: Once I allowed truncated content instead of metadata-only, the hallucination false-positive rate dropped sharply.
sentences.zh: 一旦我允许截断内容而不是仅元数据，幻觉误报率就会急剧下降。

blocks.html_en: That did not make the privacy question go away.

sentences.en: That did not make the privacy question go away.
sentences.zh: 这并没有让隐私问题消失。

blocks.html_en: It just made the tradeoff explicit.

sentences.en: It just made the tradeoff explicit.
sentences.zh: 它只是使权衡变得明确。

blocks.html_en: "Safer by default" and "useful by default" are not always the same choice.

sentences.en: "Safer by default" and "useful by default" are not always the same choice.
sentences.zh: “默认更安全”和“默认有用”并不总是相同的选择。

blocks.html_en: Structure without enough evidence is just a cleaner way to stay blind.

sentences.en: Structure without enough evidence is just a cleaner way to stay blind.
sentences.zh: 没有足够证据的结构只是一种更干净的保持盲目的方式。

blocks.html_en: I do not think enough tooling says that out loud.

sentences.en: I do not think enough tooling says that out loud.
sentences.zh: 我认为没有足够的工具大声说出这一点。

blocks.html_en: The Fifth Thing I Learned: Shipping OSS Is Not The Same As Finishing The Idea

sentences.en: The Fifth Thing I Learned: Shipping OSS Is Not The Same As Finishing The Idea
sentences.zh: 我学到的第五件事：交付 OSS 与完成想法不同

blocks.html_en: The repo is public.

sentences.en: The repo is public.
sentences.zh: 该回购协议是公开的。

blocks.html_en: The packages are published.

sentences.en: The packages are published.
sentences.zh: 软件包已发布。

blocks.html_en: The test suite is real.

sentences.en: The test suite is real.
sentences.zh: 测试套件是真实的。

blocks.html_en: The product works.

sentences.en: The product works.
sentences.zh: 该产品有效。

blocks.html_en: And I still would not call the problem solved.

sentences.en: And I still would not call the problem solved.
sentences.zh: 我仍然不认为问题已解决。

blocks.html_en: That matters to me.

sentences.en: That matters to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很重要。

blocks.html_en: I think too many OSS launch posts flatten everything into "here is what shipped" and skip "here is what I still do not trust."

sentences.en: I think too many OSS launch posts flatten everything into "here is what shipped" and skip "here is what I still do not trust."
sentences.zh: 我认为太多的 OSS 发布帖子将所有内容都扁平化为“这是已发布的内容”，并跳过“这是我仍然不信任的内容”。

blocks.html_en: Here is what I still do not trust fully:

sentences.en: Here is what I still do not trust fully:
sentences.zh: 以下是我仍然不完全信任的内容：

blocks.html_en: • the 28 detectors that have not yet fired on real corpora in a meaningful way

sentences.en: the 28 detectors that have not yet fired on real corpora in a meaningful way
sentences.zh: 尚未以有意义的方式对真实语料库进行测试的 28 个探测器

blocks.html_en: • the LLM detectors on production workloads

sentences.en: the LLM detectors on production workloads
sentences.zh: 生产工作负载上的 LLM 检测器

blocks.html_en: • span-tree materialization in the API, which is still weaker than I want

sentences.en: span-tree materialization in the API, which is still weaker than I want
sentences.zh: API 中的生成树物化，仍然比我想要的要弱

blocks.html_en: • any claim that one threshold set will generalize cleanly across workloads

sentences.en: any claim that one threshold set will generalize cleanly across workloads
sentences.zh: 任何声称设定的阈值可以在工作负载之间完全通用的说法

blocks.html_en: • any green gate that has not been proven end-to-end

sentences.en: any green gate that has not been proven end-to-end
sentences.zh: 任何尚未经过端到端验证的绿色大门

blocks.html_en: That does not mean the project should not ship.

sentences.en: That does not mean the project should not ship.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着该项目不应该发布。

blocks.html_en: It means the honest version of shipping is: this tool is useful now, and I understand its edges much better than I did when I started.

sentences.en: It means the honest version of shipping is: this tool is useful now, and I understand its edges much better than I did when I started.
sentences.zh: 这意味着运输的诚实版本是：这个工具现在很有用，而且我比刚开始时更了解它的优势。

blocks.html_en: That is a good outcome.

sentences.en: That is a good outcome.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的结果。

blocks.html_en: It is also a very different outcome from the clean version I had in my head.

sentences.en: It is also a very different outcome from the clean version I had in my head.
sentences.zh: 这也与我脑海中的干净版本有很大不同。

blocks.html_en: What I Would Do Differently Next Time

sentences.en: What I Would Do Differently Next Time
sentences.zh: 下次我会采取什么不同的做法

blocks.html_en: I would move field testing much earlier.

sentences.en: I would move field testing much earlier.
sentences.zh: 我会更早地进行现场测试。

content_html_zh:
当我开始构建agent-exec-trace时，我想我知道困难在哪里。 OSS agent-exec-trace 是 AI 代理的可观察层。 它使用 OpenTelemetry 风格的跟踪来检测代理运行，然后分析这些跟踪是否存在循环、重试风暴、成本峰值、幻觉模式和其他不良运行时行为。 目标很简单：当代理运行感觉错误时，我想要比日志和直觉更好的东西来解释原因。

我认为最困难的部分是检测器逻辑。

定义异常。 选择阈值。 连接走线。 运行分析。 发送回购协议。

这就是故事的干净版本。

真实版本更丑。

在我第一次大规模通过 Hugging Face 超过 100,000 条真实特工痕迹时，我的empty_response 探测器对其中 100% 的痕迹进行了射击。 每一条痕迹。 与此同时，我的 35 个基于规则的探测器中有 28 个根本没有触发过。

从那时起，该项目不再是“构建一些探测器”，而是转变为一种学习体验。

探测器并没有错。

痕迹的形状不对。

当我看到这一点时，许多其他的假设就被打破了。

当我运送我的特工评估安全带时，我也有一种非常相似的感觉。 不同的工具。 相同的图案。 真实的系统非常擅长破坏整洁的设计故事。

我实际上想要构建什么

我关心的问题感觉很明显。

传统的可观察性可以告诉我服务是否正常、缓慢或失败。

它无法告诉我为什么代理调用同一个工具八次，改变主意三次，在死胡同中烧掉代币，或者悄悄地陷入我永远不想在生产中重复的行为。

这种差距比人们承认的更重要。

大多数球队都会告诉你，这次跑步感觉不对。 很少有人能指出它开始出错的确切步骤。

因此，我构建了 agent-exec-trace：一个用于代理行为的 OpenTelemetry 风格的可观察层。

这个想法很简单，很容易解释。

仪器运行。 捕捉行为路径。 发出规划、工具调用、检索、内存、批准和成本的范围。 然后在这些痕迹上运行检测器，并在用户可以实际使用的 UI 中显示不良运行情况。

回购协议在这里：github.com/deghosal-2026/agent-exec-trace

它以三个 PyPI 包的形式提供，有 794 个 Python 测试和 34 个 Playwright 端到端测试，并且 SDK 故意足够小，以便有人可以包装真正的代理而无需重新设计他们的系统。

from agent_exec_trace import AgentTracer, trace_agent, tool_span

AgentTracer.setup(otlp_endpoint="http://localhost:4317")

@trace_agent(agent_name="my-agent", agent_version="1.0.0")
async def handle(query: str) -> str:
    with tool_span("search", tool_args={"q": query}):
        return await search(query)

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

那部分不是教训。

这个教训是在我有足够真实的东西可以测试之后发生的事情。

我学到的第一件事：真实痕迹的反击

我确实计划了现场测试。

只是还不够早。

这种区别很重要，因为错误不是忘记它。 错误在于将其安排得太晚，以至于系统的其余部分已经开始感觉已经完成了。

WBS 很可靠。 PRD 很彻底。 探测器目录已记录。 这些里程碑是真实的。 质量关卡很严格：ruff clean、mypy strict clean、测试绿色、覆盖率超过90%。

所有这些都是良好的纪律。

这些都没有让我免受这样一个事实：模拟特工很有礼貌，而真实的痕迹则不然。

这就是实践中“为时已晚”的情况。 当现场测试出现时，探测器目录的部分内容、有关迹线形状的假设，甚至一些里程碑门已经得到验证。 现场测试来得不够早，无法形成设计。 它来得太晚了，以至于暴露了设计在错误的现实中被验证的地方。

拥抱脸语料库是第一巴掌。

我的检测器期望在一处响应内容。 语料库以多种不同的形式存储它。 所以empty_response并没有告诉我“所有这些代理都坏了”。 它告诉我“你对迹线形状的假设太狭窄了。”

这个错误迫使四次标准化通过。 不同的响应键。 不同的工具名称约定。 不同的操作名称。 时间戳解析问题。 亲子关系不一致。

错误的验证数据不仅会产生噪音。 它充满信心地教给你错误的教训。

清理结束后，标题变得更加诚实，不再那么令人安慰。

原来的兼容性数字看起来不错。

真实的比例是42.4%。

从那时起，我不再将可观测性视为检测器问题，而是开始将其视为数据形状问题。

因为如果它所依赖的数据几乎不存在于野外，那么理论上完全正确的探测器仍然毫无用处。

我学到的第二件事：合成数据可以拯救你并误导你

一旦真实痕迹语料库向我展示了它的局限性，我就转向了另一个方向。

我构建了一个合成跟踪生成器。

一百万条痕迹。 十个假特工。 十四个工具。 故意行为模式：循环、重试、超时、不活动间隙、干预等待、令牌爆炸、内存突发。

这立即解决了一个问题。

结构兼容性跃升至99.2%。

现在探测器有了他们可以实际看到的东西。

35 个基于规则的探测器中有 20 个被发射。

听起来像是一场胜利。 确实如此。

但合成数据却以不同的方式存在。

我的幻觉探测器探测到了 98% 的合成痕迹。 不是因为我无意中构建了历史上最伟大的探测器，而是因为合成输出和合成工具证据之间存在虚假关系，使得探测器的工作变得过于简单。

成本方面也发生了同样的情况。 我的 cost_spike 检测器有一个真正的阈值。 我的合成发电机产生的成本大部分是美分级的。 所以探测器也几乎从未在那里发射过。

合成痕迹可以证明探测器正在运行。 他们无法证明这很重要。

这给了我第二堂我急需的课：

合成迹线非常适合证明探测器可以运行。

它们不足以证明探测器已针对现实进行了校准。

所以现在我想到了分层验证。

单元测试告诉我逻辑是有效的。

合成痕迹告诉我探测器可以看到它需要的字段。

真实的痕迹告诉我这些在我自己的沙箱之外是否重要。

当写下来时，这个顺序听起来很明显。 当我正在构建它的时候，感觉并不明显。

我学到的第三件事：绿色之门可能会说谎

这个问题比任何探测器错误都更让我恼火。

我已将 OTLP 导出里程碑标记为已完成。

大门是绿色的。

文档看起来不错。

演示看起来不错。

而且端到端的导出路径从未被实际验证过。

两个 bug 互相抵消了。

OTel 收集器的 gRPC 端口未在 Docker Compose 中公开。

我使用配置的本地跟踪而不是 OTLP 导出的 SDK 路径。

因此，我为一项尚未真正发挥作用的功能完成了里程碑。

这是比考试失败更糟糕的教训。

失败的测试是诚实的。

由两个取消错误创建的绿色门在某种程度上看起来是不诚实的。

这改变了我对里程碑的看法。

我现在不再信任绿色复选标记了。

如果门无法证明真实代理发出、Jaeger 接收、分析摄取以及 API 提供结果，则门是不完整的。 我不在乎之前通过了多少次检查。

这不仅仅是一个可观察性的课程。 这只是软件工程。

我学到的第四件事：没有内容的结构是不够的

我一开始对隐私相当保守。

仅元数据感到有责任。

没有原始工具参数。 没有完整的工具响应。 默认情况下没有内存值。

合理的本能。

但它教会了我一个更不舒服的权衡。

仅捕获结构的可观察性 SDK 可能会在您最需要判断的地方变得盲目。

我的幻觉探测器就是最明显的例子。

如果检测器无法看到工具返回的内容，则无法有意义地判断特工的声明是否与证据相符。

一旦我允许截断内容而不是仅元数据，幻觉误报率就会急剧下降。

这并没有让隐私问题消失。

它只是使权衡变得明确。

“默认更安全”和“默认有用”并不总是相同的选择。

没有足够证据的结构只是一种更干净的保持盲目的方式。

我认为没有足够的工具大声说出这一点。

我学到的第五件事：交付 OSS 与完成想法不同

该回购协议是公开的。

软件包已发布。

测试套件是真实的。

该产品有效。

我仍然不认为问题已解决。

这对我来说很重要。

我认为太多的 OSS 发布帖子将所有内容都扁平化为“这是已发布的内容”，并跳过“这是我仍然不信任的内容”。

以下是我仍然不完全信任的内容：

  • 尚未以有意义的方式对真实语料库进行测试的 28 个探测器
  • 生产工作负载上的 LLM 检测器
  • API 中的生成树物化，仍然比我想要的要弱
  • 任何声称设定的阈值可以在工作负载之间完全通用的说法
  • 任何尚未经过端到端验证的绿色大门

这并不意味着该项目不应该发布。

这意味着运输的诚实版本是：这个工具现在很有用，而且我比刚开始时更了解它的优势。

这是一个很好的结果。

这也与我脑海中的干净版本有很大不同。

下次我会采取什么不同的做法

我会更早地进行现场测试。

不是因为我没有想到，而是因为计划和提前计划不是一回事。

后期现场测试变成审核。 早期的现场测试决定了设计。

当我的运行时，它已经强大到足以揭露错误的假设，但为时已晚，无法阻止我在它们之上建立信心。

我会将跟踪语料库视为设计工件，而不仅仅是测试输入。

我会更早地坚持端到端的烟雾路径。

我不会再假装检测器逻辑是问题的中心。

显然，这很重要。

但建立这个之后，我认为更难的问题是：

  • 你的痕迹实际上能看到什么？
  • 野外数据有多奇怪？
  • 你的探测器在结构上取决于什么？
  • 你怎么知道绿门是真的？

这就是这个项目给我的实际教育。

不是“如何编写 40 个检测器”。

更像是：在 40 个探测器产生任何意义之前，还有多少其他事情必须是真实的。

也许最难的一点是：从未触发过真实痕迹的探测器还没有真正完成。 它刚刚经过充分测试。

开放讨论

我真的很喜欢从业者对此的抵制。
